title: Tender: Accelerating Large Language Models via Tensor Decomposition and Runtime Requantization
problem: LLM inference deployment faces challenges from high compute and memory requirements due to massive model sizes, combined with difficulty running models in low-precision integer pipelines while managing outlier values that complicate quantization.
motivation: Large language models are now critical workloads in computing systems, making efficient inference deployment essential for practical large-scale deployment.
method: Tender decomposes large matrices into smaller pieces and quantizes each with its own scale factor (a multiplier for converting to lower precision). To avoid expensive requantization—converting back to full precision and re-quantizing—when combining partial sums, the scale factors are chosen as powers of two. This works because multiplying by powers of two is just bit-shifting in computers, which costs almost nothing. The approach needs only minor hardware modifications.
key_novelty: Making scale factors powers of two apart in decomposed matrices to eliminate requantization when combining partial sums.
contributions: Decomposed quantization technique specifically optimized for low-precision LLM inference
Analysis of outlier value patterns in LLMs and quantization implications
Minimal hardware extensions for commodity tensor accelerators
Algorithm-hardware co-design achieving higher accuracy and inference performance than state-of-the-art

metrics.speedup: improved inference performance compared to state-of-the-art

primary_theme: low-precision LLM acceleration via tensor decomposition
